title: API Gateway
subtitle: Centralizing cross-cutting edge concerns—TLS termination, JWT validation, rate limiting, routing, and the Backend-for-Frontend (BFF) pattern.
keyTakeaways: An API Gateway is the single L7 entry point for external clients, offloading cross-cutting concerns (AuthN, Rate Limiting, WAF, TLS, Observability) from internal microservices.
The **Backend-for-Frontend (BFF)** pattern deploys tailored gateway layers per client type (Mobile BFF vs Web BFF vs Public API) to optimize payload shapes and aggregation.
Never put heavy business logic or synchronous cross-service orchestration loops inside a monolithic shared API Gateway, or it becomes an organizational bottleneck and SPOF.

sections.heading: 1. Architectural Fundamentals & Core Mechanics
sections.body: API Gateway is a foundational architectural concept in distributed systems. Centralizing cross-cutting edge concerns—TLS termination, JWT validation, rate limiting, routing, and the Backend-for-Frontend (BFF) pattern. Fundamentally, Without an API Gateway, every single client app (iOS, Android, Web) would need to know the hostnames of 50 internal microservices, and every single microservice team would have to re-implement TLS termination, OAuth JWT validation, IP rate limiting, CORS headers, and access logging across 5 different programming languages. An API Gateway (such as Kong, AWS API Gateway, Envoy, or Apigee) consolidates these cross-cutting edge concerns into a hardened, horizontally scaled proxy tier.
bullets: **Core Architectural Principle**: An API Gateway is the single L7 entry point for external clients, offloading cross-cutting concerns (AuthN, Rate Limiting, WAF, TLS, Observability) from internal microservices.

**Problem Space & Invariants**: The **Backend-for-Frontend (BFF)** pattern deploys tailored gateway layers per client type (Mobile BFF vs Web BFF vs Public API) to optimize payload shapes and aggregation.
**System Boundary**: Operates across client network dispatch, gateway queuing, thread execution pools, and persistent storage I/O.

sections.heading: 2. Architectural Patterns & Implementation Topologies
sections.body: In production distributed systems, api gateway manifests across several distinct architectural classifications, operational modes, and implementation strategies:
bullets: **Single Centralized API Gateway (Kong / Envoy / AWS API GW)**: Focuses on uniform security, rate limiting, tls, and observability across the entire company; simple single domain (`api.company.com`) for clients. Best suited for Cross-cutting edge security, routing, rate limiting, and public developer APIs..

**Edge Gateway + Client-Specific BFFs (Mobile BFF, Web BFF)**: Focuses on frontend and mobile teams iterate autonomously on payload aggregation; reduces chatty mobile round-trips over cellular networks. Best suited for Organizations with distinct Web, iOS/Android, TV, and Public API experiences consuming a large microservice fleet..

1. Authentication Offload: Validates the client's JWT signature (using cached JWKS public keys) at the edge and forwards verified internal identity headers (`X-User-Id`, `X-Tenant-Id`) or an internal token to upstream services.
2. Rate Limiting & Quota Enforcement: Enforces per-tenant and per-IP token buckets before malicious traffic reaches internal compute.
Mobile BFF: Strips unnecessary fields, merges 4 internal gRPC calls via `Promise.allSettled()`, and formats payloads for mobile UI components.

Partial Failure Resilience: If the internal Recommendation Service times out during BFF aggregation, the BFF still returns 200 OK with the user's orders and an empty `recommendations: []` fallback array.

sections.heading: 3. Production Strengths: Where & How to Apply
sections.body: Adopting appropriate design patterns around api gateway unlocks critical performance, scalability, and operational advantages for modern backend platforms:
bullets: **Where to Use — High-Impact Scenarios**: Optimal for Cross-cutting edge security, routing, rate limiting, and public developer APIs. and environments requiring Uniform security, rate limiting, TLS, and observability across the entire company; simple single domain (`api.company.com`) for clients..

**Where to Use — High-Throughput Scenarios**: Recommended for Organizations with distinct Web, iOS/Android, TV, and Public API experiences consuming a large microservice fleet. where Frontend and mobile teams iterate autonomously on payload aggregation; reduces chatty mobile round-trips over cellular networks..

**How to Use — Engineering Implementation**: A mobile app on a 3G connection wants a single compact endpoint (`GET /mobile/home-screen`) that aggregates user profile, unread notification count, and top 5 feed items in 2KB. Always establish explicit thresholds, measurement baselines, and automated monitoring.
**Architectural Leverage**: Provides predictable resource boundaries, bounds blast radius, and optimizes cost per transaction.

sections.heading: 4. Failure Modes & Trade-Offs: When to Avoid
sections.body: While essential for scalable engineering, api gateway introduces substantial architectural trade-offs, operational failure modes, and anti-patterns if applied inappropriately:
bullets: **Where to Avoid — Trade-Off Bottlenecks**: Avoid when constraints impose adds an extra network hop (~1-2ms); can become a deployment bottleneck if teams put custom business logic or complex transformations inside it.
**Where to Avoid — Complexity Ceiling**: Avoid premature optimization when some duplication of aggregation code across web bff and mobile bff; more deployables to monitor.
**Catastrophic Failure Modes**: Uncalibrated parameters can trigger queue exhaustion, thread starvation, cascading retry storms, and tail latency amplification.
**Operational Overhead**: Requires continuous observability (p95/p99 latency tracking, saturation alerts, and distributed tracing across hop boundaries).

sections.heading: 5. Staff+ Engineering Verdict & Interview Playbook
sections.body: Mastering api gateway is a defining trait of Staff-level distributed systems engineers. Navigating the delicate balance between performance, reliability, and simplicity ensures architectures scale sustainably without introducing unmanageable operational friction.
bullets: **Staff+ Golden Rule**: Never put heavy business logic or synchronous cross-service orchestration loops inside a monolithic shared API Gateway, or it becomes an organizational bottleneck and SPOF.

**Staff+ Interview Playbook**: When placing an API Gateway in your architecture diagram, explicitly list the **exact order of operations** it performs: (1) TLS Termination -> (2) IP/WAF Filter -> (3) JWT Auth Validation -> (4) Rate Limiting -> (5) L7 Routing.

tradeOffs.cons: Some duplication of aggregation code across Web BFF and Mobile BFF; more deployables to monitor.
tradeOffs.bestFor: Organizations with distinct Web, iOS/Android, TV, and Public API experiences consuming a large microservice fleet.
